function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I can’t pull live data from Amazon for you. However, I can walk you through the steps you can take to find the price and shipping policy for the Galaxy S24 on Amazon yourself: | Step | What to do | Tips | |------|------------|------| | 1 | **Open Amazon** | Go to (or your local Amazon site). | | 2 | **Search for “Galaxy S24”** | Use the search bar at the top of the page. | | 3 | **Select the correct listing** | Look for the official Samsung listing or a reputable seller. | | 4 | **Check the price** | The price is displayed prominently under the product title. | | 5 | **Look for “Add to Cart” / “Buy Now”** | Hover over or click the button to see if it says “Prime” or “Free Shipping.” | | 6 | **View shipping details** | Click the “See all buying options” link (if available) or scroll down to the “Shipping” section. | | 7 | **Read the shipping policy** | Amazon will list:
• Shipping speed (e.g., “Prime – 2‑day shipping”)
• Shipping cost (free or paid)
• Any restrictions (e.g., “Ships only to the U.S.”). | | 8 | **Check seller’s policy** | If it’s a third‑party seller, click the seller’s name to view their shipping terms. | | 9 | **Compare prices** | Use the “Compare with other sellers” link to see if other sellers offer lower prices or better shipping. | ### Quick Tips - **Prime Badge**: If the product has a Prime badge, you’ll usually get free, fast shipping (often 2‑day or same‑day in some regions). - **“Free Shipping”**: Even without Prime, many sellers offer free shipping if you meet a minimum purchase amount. - **Seller Ratings**: Look at the seller’s rating and reviews; higher ratings often correlate with reliable shipping. - **Amazon’s “Shipping & Returns” Section**: Scroll to the bottom of the product page; there’s a “Shipping & Returns” link that gives a concise summary. If you’re building a bot or script, Amazon’s official **Product Advertising API** (PA API) is the proper way to retrieve product information programmatically. You’ll need to register for an Amazon Associates account, obtain access keys, and then query the API for the ASIN of the Galaxy S24. The API returns JSON that includes price, availability, and shipping details. Let me know if you’d like a quick example of how to call the PA API or if you have any other questions!
